title: Bench-to-Dollar Playbook: Performance Claims & Evidence Matrix
summary: Working playbook for converting lab microbenchmarks into defensible go-to-market claims about latency-per-cost and tokens-per-dollar. Focused on repeatable methodology, evidence tiers, and guardrails for marketing and sales language.
body:
Purpose
This doc is a pragmatic bridge between engineering bench outputs and GTM-friendly claims. It focuses on a small set of tightly defined, reproducible claims (latency-to-cost deltas, tokens-per-dollar) plus the minimum evidence required to publish them externally.

Audience
- Field sales/BD: short, provable claims to use in demos and proposals.
- Marketing: phrasing and guardrails for web copy and datasheets.
- Engineering/RnD: a checklist for what to run to validate claims.

High-level claim framework (single-sentence patterns)
- "For production chat workloads, Redwood reduces median per-request inference cost by X–Yx vs. competitor baseline while meeting p95 latency <= Z ms for 8k context."
- "Applications with 95% prefix reuse see >N tokens/$ when using Redwood’s KV cache + batching vs. baseline endpoint."

Priority claims we want to prove (ordered)
1) Cost-per-token advantage for realistic chat workloads (mix of short prompts + long context). Evidence tier: lab runs + 2 customer pilots + bill-extrapolation.
2) Tail-latency stability (p99/p95) under mixed burst load (webchat + async background). Evidence tier: stress tests, SLO traces from Dedicated customer.
3) Effective throughput (tokens/sec/$) when using prefix caching + continuous batching vs stateless endpoints. Evidence tier: benchmark harness + one partner deployment.

Bench methodology (minimum reproducible test)
- Workloads: three canonical profiles: (A) short-turn chat (avg gen len 50 tokens, seq 1k), (B) long-context assistant (avg gen len 200 tokens, seq 8k), (C) reranking/embeddings microcalls (avg 30 tokens, high qps).
- Models: pick 2 open variants we ship (e.g., redwood-v1-7b, redwood-v1-13b-quant). Include a smaller and a midsize model.
- Hardware baseline: compare our Dedicated config (A100/RTX equivalent) against competitor-managed endpoint (document instance type). Always include absolute instance SKU and hourly price used in calculation.
- Runtime config: batch sizes observed in production distributions, KV cache enabled/disabled, quantization profile used, tokenization settings.
- Measurement: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and effective tokens-per-dollar (tokens generated per $ of infra during run).
- Repeats: run each workload 5x at 95% CI; capture standard deviation; if std dev >10%, run 10x.

Cost model notes (how to compute tokens-per-dollar)
- Use marketplace or cloud list price for VM/GPU + 25% infra overhead (networking, NVMe, reserved licensing). Document all assumptions.
- Formula: tokens-per-dollar = total_tokens_generated / total_infra_cost_during_run. If multi-tenant inference used, attribute cost via measured GPU utilization ratio.
- Cache-adjusted cost: track cache hit ratio; effective cost per generated token = infra_cost / (generated_tokens + cache_hits * avg_saved_tokens).

Evidence tiers (what we show externally)
- Tier 1 (Public): lab benchmark summary graphs, clear test parameters, caveats. Suitable for datasheet and website.
- Tier 2 (Field): internal benchmark + anonymized customer pilot delta numbers. Suitable for sales one-pagers and RFP attachments.
- Tier 3 (Confidential): full reproducible artifacts (scripts, raw logs, cloud bills) for enterprise due diligence. Only with NDA.

Competitive framing guidance (do / don't)
- Do: compare against clearly specified baseline (instance type, model version, config).
- Do: call out when fallback models were used to meet latency SLOs.
- Don't: claim "cheaper" in absolute terms without disclosing workload and cache assumptions. Avoid broad statements like "X% cheaper for all use cases."
- Don't: cherry-pick single short-turn benchmarks and present as general-purpose improvement.

Sample claim + supporting text for marketing (approved wording draft)
"In real-world chat workloads with sustained prefix reuse, Redwood can deliver up to 3x more useful tokens per dollar than unmanaged endpoints by combining KV caching, adaptive batching, and quantization-aware kernels. Benchmarks reflect our Dedicated config vs. baseline endpoint under reproducible test conditions (see datasheet link)."
Guardrail sentence: "Claims reflect specific workloads — results vary by prompt mix, context length, and cacheable prefix ratio."

Customer-facing proof appendix (what we attach)
- Short technical appendix (1 page): workload description, model versions, instance SKUs, exact runtime flags.
- Graphs: tokens/$ vs qps, p50/p95 latency curves across load, cache-hit sensitivity chart.
- One-sentence customer quote (if pilot): "We cut inference spend by ~35% in our assistant pipeline while reducing p95 from 420ms to 220ms" — anonymized.

Internal validation checklist before externalizing a claim
- [ ] Bench harness repo + commit hash attached.
- [ ] Cloud bill or price table used is included.
- [ ] Repro script runs documented and passes smoke checks.
- [ ] CI artifacts: perf logs, GPU metrics, raw tokens counts.
- [ ] Legal/Compliance review for public claim language (contact: Legal).
- [ ] One internal engineering sign-off and one Go-to-Market sign-off.

Open questions / TODOs
- Need a small matrix mapping common customer workloads (support chat, code assist, search summaries) to the three canonical profiles above — Priya to draft by 2025-03-10.
- Define standard competitor baseline SKUs we will use for public claims (Ollie/R&D owns).
- Run cold-start vs warm-KV scenarios and capture warmup curve (JIRA-1214).

Next steps and owners
- Perf team: run the three canonical profiles on redwood-v1-7b and redwood-v1-13b-quant and upload artifacts (owner: Omar, target: 2025-03-12).
- GTM: draft datasheet copy and 1-page appendix using Tier 1 evidence (owner: Liam, target: 2025-03-17).
- Legal: review proposed copy and guardrails (owner: Maya, target: 2025-03-19).

Notes (record of rapid thoughts)
- Keep claims directional and tied to tokens-per-dollar since customers understand $/API-call but often need tokens-per-dollar to plan scale.
- Avoid brand-to-brand naming in public materials; use "typical unmanaged endpoint" or anonymized competitor buckets.
- For sales playbooks, produce short scripts that translate a tokens/$ number into monthly spend examples for a 1M-turns/month app.

End of working draft.
Feedback welcome — add comments inline or ping on #g2m-perf.
